title: Problems on Ages
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Problems on Ages. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

coverage: Present, past and future age expressions

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Use one reference time

Choose present ages as variables. If a person is x years old now, the age after t years is x+t and the age t years ago is x-t. The difference between two people's ages stays constant; their ratio changes with time.

Translate the relationships

A is twice B means (\(A=2B\)), while A is 2 years older than B means (\(A=B+2\)). Keep the reference time explicit: five years ago A was twice B is (\(A-5=2(B-5)\)), not (\(A-5=2B\)). Solve the equations and verify every condition at its stated time.

Worked example: A and B total 40 now. Five years ago A was twice B: (\(A+B=40\)) and (\(A-5=2(B-5)\)). The solution is (\(A=25, B=15\)); five years ago they were 20 and 10.

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• Make a present/past/future table before forming equations.
  • When ages shift by the same amount, shift each age before comparing ratios.
  • Use the constant age difference as a quick check.
  • For three people, define only independent ages and express the rest from sums or differences.
  • Reject solutions that imply an impossible negative age at the stated time.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• After t years: x+t. t years ago: x-t.
  • Age difference is invariant: (\(A+t\))-(\(B+t\))=A-B.
  • Age ratio is generally not invariant.
  • Substitute the solution into every original condition.

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    A and B together are 40 years old. Five years ago, A was twice B's age. What are their present ages?

    1. A 25, B 15
    2. A 30, B 10
    3. A 24, B 16
    4. A 20, B 20
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: A 25, B 15

    Let their present ages be (\(A,B\)). Then (\(A+B=40\)) and (\(A-5=2(B-5)\)), so (\(A=2B-5\)). Hence (\(3B=45\)), (\(B=15\)), and (\(A=25\)).

  2. Core:

    A parent is three times a child's age. In 12 years, the parent will be twice the child's age. How old is the child now?

    1. (\(8\))
    2. (\(10\))
    3. (\(12\))
    4. (\(14\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(12\))

    Let the child be (\(x\)); the parent is (\(3x\)). Then (\(3x+12=2(x+12)\)), giving (\(x=12\)).

  3. Foundation:

    Two present ages sum to 39. In 5 years, their ages will be in the ratio (\(4:3\)). What are their present ages?

    1. 23 and 16
    2. 24 and 15
    3. 21 and 18
    4. 25 and 14
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: 23 and 16

    Their future sum is 49. With ratio 4:3, the future ages are 28 and 21; subtract 5 to get 23 and 16.

  4. Standard:

    A father is three times his child's age now. Four years ago, he was five times the child's age. How old is the child now?

    1. (\(6\))
    2. (\(8\))
    3. (\(10\))
    4. (\(12\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(8\))

    Let the child's age be c; the father is 3c. Four years ago: (\(3c-4=5(c-4)\)). Thus (\(16=2c\)), so c=8.

  5. Challenge:

    A is 6 years older than B. Four years from now, their ages will sum to 42. What are their current ages?

    1. 17 and 11
    2. 18 and 12
    3. 19 and 13
    4. 20 and 14
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: 20 and 14

    Their present sum is (\(42-8=34\)). With difference 6, the ages are (\((34+6)/2=20\)) and (\((34-6)/2=14\)).
